questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Kultur og relevante fag.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Meget af den information der er på deres hjemmeside kan bruges, men er nogle gange lidt svært at forstå hvordan det skal bruges. Men lige før man starter bliver der holdt nogle forskellige oplæg, hvor man får meget information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Lige før man starter får man en masse information. Der er både en studenterforening der hjælper, og kontoret der er tilknyttet. Skriv til kontoret på UTokyo hvis man har nogle spørgsmål.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: UTokyo har nogle kollegier tilknyttet som man kan søge. Dette er relativt nemt, men du er ikke sikret en plads.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Nogle kollegier er dyre, nogle er billigere. De ligge ret spredt ud i byen, så hvis du vil have et billigt, så kan det være du ender med at skulle bruge 45 min til en time på at komme på campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Hvis jeg skulle gøre det igen, ville jeg finde mig et sharehouse og bo i.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Meget lang og ret kompliceret. Man skal udfylde helt vild mange dokumenter fordi Japan ikke er særlig digitaliseret og moderniseret. Dermed overfører de ikke basal data til hinanden, og du skal dermed udfylde informationer for alle forskellige servicer og institutioner.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Du kan læse om noget af det på hjemmesiden, men er ikke så godt. Skriv heller til UTokyo kontoret, de er meget behjælpelige og svare hurtigt.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Jeg fik alle de fag jeg gerne ville have.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Det er lidt en kamp, men bliv ved og så skal det nok lykkes. Husk at være opmærksom på at du udfylder de rigtige informationer, da Japanerne ikke er så fleksible hvis du skriver noget forkert.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Københavns niveau er bedre end her, selv om de bolstre sig med at de er et af de bedste i Asien. Så bare rolig.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Der er flere oplæg og aktiv deltagelse, men det er som oftes også en del af karakteren. Man kan også godt finde fag der er mere forelæsnings orienterede.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Public Policy and Energi
Policy Process and Negotiations
Public Policy and Politics
Energy Security
International Energy Security

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Hvis man er interesseret i mere policy level klima og energi så tag de fag jeg tog. Ellers syntes jeg også Policy Process and Negotiations var ret godt da man lærte ret mange ting. 
Overordnet har jeg ikke arbejdet så meget med policy så syntes jeg havde en ret stejl læringskurve.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Hvis man gerne vil rejse rundt i Japan, og her gerne bruge Shinkansen, så regn med at bruge mange penge da det er ret så dyrt.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Mad og øl. Man spiser ret meget ude da der er så mange gode steder at spise til billige penge.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Der er rigtig mange klubber, men de er alle sammen japansk talene. Så hvis man vil være en del af dem så skal du kunne japansk.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Jeg klatre ret meget, så jeg blev gode venner med nogle nede i min lokale klatreklub.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Der er rigtig mange steder, både dagsture og weekendturer. Næsten alle steder er nice. Men tag nok op i bjergene, da det er meget rart at komme ud af byen en gang imellem.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Det er nemt nok. Du får flere passes når du ikke er japaner, men altså der er mange ting man lige skal vende sig til.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Det kan godt blive lidt svært, da selv universitetet studerende japanere er meget dårlige til engelsk. Dog på min skole er der også en god sjat fra EU og andre engelsk talende lande.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: At Japanerne er dårlige til engelsk.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Mad, venlighed, renlighed, æstetik og mærkelighed.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Vær parat på at hvis du gerne vil blive gode venner med Japaner skal du Japansk. Underviserne er mere engegeret i dig, og vil gerne hjælpe dig med din fremtidige karrierer. Husk ikke at blive taget af den japanske arbejdsetik.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Det er et fantastisk land, tag ud og spis en masse mærkelig mad, drik nogle øl med venner.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Nye venskaber og nye måder at se verden på

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Japansk undervisning - det er pisse svært

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
